gaps.lead: I can't wait for the holidays to start.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: the 'to' is a preposition.

gaps.lead: I always hated pasta when I was a child, but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.sentence: I ___ pasta when I was a child but now I cook it regularly.
gaps.explanation: 'used to + infinitive' describes a past state or habit that is no longer true.

gaps.lead: Someone must check this equipment before every flight.
gaps.explanation: must check → must be checked (modal + be + past participle).

gaps.lead: Simon really ought to make a decision about his future.
gaps.sentence: It's high time Simon ___ about his future.
gaps.hint: it's high time + past; make a decision = make up one's mind
gaps.explanation: 'It's high time' takes the past subjunctive: 'made up his mind'.

gaps.lead: She started working here five years ago.
gaps.explanation: Action continuing from a past point to now: has been working (present perfect continuous).

gaps.lead: It's very unlikely that Martin will win the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.sentence: Martin has almost ___ the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.explanation: 'It's very unlikely he will win' becomes 'he has almost no chance of winning'.
